ECE 6390

G/T and link margin

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows the running 10 GHz geostationary downlink to a 1 m dish, carried from EIRP to C/N₀ and then compared with the Eb/N₀ that uncoded QPSK needs at a 10⁻⁶ bit-error rate.

A downlink budget in decibels adds the satellite EIRP, subtracts free-space and atmospheric losses, adds the receive gain, and compares the result with the receiver noise. Writing the noise density as N₀ = k_B·T_sys groups the two receiver quantities into one figure of merit: C/N₀ = EIRP − L_FS − L_atm + G/T − 10·log₁₀k_B, with G/T = G_r − 10·log₁₀T_sys in dB/K and −10·log₁₀k_B = 228.6 dB.

G/T rewards antenna gain and penalizes noise together. Doubling the dish diameter adds 6.02 dB of gain at fixed efficiency; doubling the system noise temperature removes 3.01 dB. Gain and temperature must refer to the same receiver plane, usually the antenna output.

Dividing by the bit rate converts C/N₀ to energy per bit: Eb/N₀ = C/N₀ − 10·log₁₀R_b. The link margin is the amount by which this exceeds the Eb/N₀ that the modulation, coding and target error rate require. A positive margin is the allowance available for rain fades, pointing error and implementation loss; a negative margin means the link does not close.

Each lever acts at a definite point. EIRP and antenna size act before the noise, rain attenuation subtracts from C/N₀, and a lower bit rate trades throughput for Eb/N₀ decibel for decibel. Coding lowers the requirement instead, by its coding gain.

Example

EIRP 40 dBW, free-space loss 203.82 dB and a 1 m dish of 38.19 dBi with T_sys = 290 K give G/T = 13.56 dB/K and C/N₀ = 40 − 203.82 + 13.56 + 228.60 = 78.34 dB-Hz. At 4 Mbit/s, Eb/N₀ = 12.32 dB, about 1.8 dB above the 10.5 dB that uncoded QPSK needs at 10⁻⁶. A 2 dB rain fade would close the link only with coding.

Practice

1. The ground station replaces its 1 m dish with a 2 m dish and keeps T_sys = 290 K. How do G/T and the margin change?

Gain scales with diameter squared at fixed efficiency.

Gain and G/T rise by 20·log₁₀2 ≈ 6.02 dB, so C/N₀, Eb/N₀ and the margin all rise by 6.02 dB, to about 7.8 dB.

2. At fixed C/N₀, how much must the bit rate fall to recover a 3 dB rain fade?

Use Eb/N₀ = C/N₀ − 10·log₁₀R_b.

Halving the bit rate adds 3.01 dB of Eb/N₀, recovering the fade at the cost of half the throughput.
